title: Panes are a split tree with anchored and transient panes
body:
`src/panes.rs` holds three fixed rectangles and a focused index. A new window
takes the first free pane whose app id matches, and a pane whose client exits
keeps its rectangle.

## Proposal

A binary split tree: a leaf is a pane, a node is a horizontal or vertical
split with a ratio. `arrange` walks it over the body and gives every pane a
cell rectangle whose outer ring is its outline; the client gets the inside.

Two kinds of pane. An anchor has a name and a rule, today an app id, and
stays as an empty slot saying "waiting for <rule>" when its client exits.
A transient pane is removed when its client exits and its sibling takes the
space. The three panes of today become anchors for `decade.chat`,
`decade.terminal` and `decade.code`.

Placement at a window's first commit: the empty anchor whose rule matches
the app id; otherwise a new transient pane split off the focused pane along
its longer side. Ctrl+Shift+Enter makes a transient pane the same way and
starts a shell in it, named terminal2, terminal3 and so on; the ghostty is
started with that name as its class so it lands there.

The router addresses panes by name rather than index, since indices move
when the tree changes.

## Out of scope

- Rules other than an app id. Wildcard and typed rules come with anchors
  over MCP.
